newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Acer unit says no impact from FDA flap.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Acer unit says no impact from FDA flap.

text.p: Taiwan computer monitor maker Acer Peripherals said Monday a threatened U.S. import ban caused it briefly to halt shipments to the United States but that the dispute had been resolved and no lasting impact was likely.

A spokeswoman said an Acer Peripherals plant in Taoyuan halted shipments for "two or three days" after the U.S. Food and Drug Administration on Oct. 19 told Acer it had found deficiencies in the firm's radiation testing procedures.
The issue was quickly resolved through consultations.
"The FDA gave us the clearing on Oct. 26," spokeswoman Chen Tsai-wen said. "Shipments to the United States have already resumed and we don't expect any changes in sales."
"The news of FDA not issuing a ban is obviously good for Acer Peripherals and one that boosts investor confidence in the company," Foremost Investment broker Wang Jieh said.
The FDA's Oct. 19 notice threatened to ban imports of Acer monitors if the testing deficiencies were not resolved in 15 days, prompting Acer to suspend shipments voluntarily.
The FDA dropped the threat after Acer Peripherals showed it had complied with U.S. quality-control requirements, the company said.

Chen said that only the Taoyuan plant, which produces 50,000 monitors a month, was questioned by the FDA, while its main plant in Malaysia, with monthly capacity of 200,000 monitors, had not come under scrutiny.

"Most of our exports to the U.S. come out of the Malaysian plant, while the Taoyuan plant exports only about 10,000 monitors to the U.S. per month. So the scale of influence is very small," Chen said.
Acer Peripherals has consistently said the discrepancy was over methods of testing and reporting, denying that its popular monitors were dangerous.
Chen said Acer Peripherals would abide by FDA radiation testing guidelines in the future in order to avoid further shipment delays.
Acer Peripherals is a key member of Acer group and is the world's third-largest maker of colour monitors. It has factories in Taiwan, Malaysia and China.
In 1995, combined revenues at parent Acer group totalled $5.8 billion.
